summary.intent: Explore protocol improvements for the cipher-box platform post-v1.1, specifically around operation idempotency, ACID patterns, and social-graph privacy (blinding the write-share owner→recipient edge).
summary.outcome: Discovered that IPNS write authorization is entirely cryptographic (key possession), not server-enforced — invalidating an earlier assumption that write-shares couldn't be blinded. Seven artifacts were created (1 note, 1 seed, 5 bug todos) and committed to a new `docs/explore-protocol-and-privacy-hardening` branch with a PR in progress.

repo: IPNS write authorization is purely cryptographic: a valid signed record = authorization. The server never verifies Ed25519 signatures on publish.
`findActiveWriteShare` is a DB-row routing convenience (redirecting a recipient's publish onto the owner's canonical row), not a security boundary. The resolve path ignores the social edge entirely.
The server self-increments the IPNS sequence number instead of reading it from the client-supplied signed record, which is the root of sequence-divergence bugs acknowledged in a code comment.

Write-share social graph can be fully blinded; keying records by `ipnsName` instead of `userId` and verifying the record signature would make the protocol self-authorizing and simultaneously fix the sequence-integrity bug.
An existing todo (`2026-02-22-crdt-ipns-inbox-sharing.md`) already explores a CRDT inbox for serverless share discovery — the new finding sharpens its scope significantly.
Five acute high-severity bugs (security + data loss) exist independently of any redesign: cross-user unpin, quota never decremented, FUSE release data-loss, mkdir orphan, and 409 retry lost-update.
lint-staged runs prettier over markdown on commit.

code.finding: Optional check that publicKey derives to ipnsName, but Ed25519 signature on the record is never verified.
Write-share lookup redirects recipient's publish onto the owner's DB row — routing, not authorization.
Server self-increments sequence number instead of reading it from the signed record, causing sequence divergence.
Canonical IPNS row keyed by (userId, ipnsName) via getFolderIpns — the structural reason write-shares need DB-row routing.
Resolve path keys by ipnsName alone; never consults the social edge.
Code comment acknowledging the sequence-divergence bug.
POST /ipfs/unpin has no ownership check — any authenticated user can unpin any CID. Security bug.
recordUnpin has zero callers; storage quota grows monotonically and never decrements on unpin.
FUSE release() returns OK to OS then zeroizes/deletes the temp file before remote commit completes — crash after ack = silent permanent data loss.
mkdir never queues parent for republish; folder disappears on restart (macOS path — line number flagged as unverified, needs grep before fixing).
409 conflict retry re-resolves only the sequence number and republishes stale children, silently overwriting a concurrent writer's changes.

workflow: The GSD explore workflow requires reading questioning.md and domain-probes.md before starting, then fans out parallel research agents per subsystem.
Artifacts are cross-linked by slug (e.g. seed references existing todo) to avoid duplication and surface related work.
When the working tree contains pre-existing uncommitted changes, stage by explicit pathspec rather than `git add -A` to avoid accidentally including unrelated work.
Mixed-content commits (planning docs + lockfile + test files) on a docs/ branch are acceptable to the user if the content is related to a single exploration session.

Assistant made an incorrect assumption (write-shares can't be blinded) before reading the actual code — required a correction pass after the user pushed back.
The research agents' summaries were not fully trustworthy and needed direct code verification to correct.
